THE YMCA OF MONTREAL'S OWN WEBSITE, 1999-2012, IN THE INTERNET ARCHIVE
Inventory built 2026-09-07 with archive.org's availability API, which works
here while web.archive.org does not (f_5361). NOTHING BELOW HAS BEEN READ.

=====================================================================
WHY THIS IS WORTH SOMEBODY'S AFTERNOON
=====================================================================

This project's coverage of Kanawana in the 2000s is among its thinnest, and
the association published its own camp pages every spring in exactly those
years. A camp's website in JUNE carries that summer's session dates, age
bands, fees, programme names and often its director -- the things the wiki has
had to reconstruct from brochures, alumni recollection and the occasional
annual report.

AND THE CAPTURES SIT ALMOST EXACTLY ON JUNE, YEAR AFTER YEAR.

=====================================================================
THE RUN: ymcamontreal.qc.ca, front page, closest capture to 1 June
=====================================================================

  1999-10-13   2000-06-20   2001-05-16   2002-05-30   2003-05-29
  2004-06-06   2005-06-02   2006-06-13   2007-06-12   2008-06-07
  2009-06-01   2010-06-12   2011-07-06   2012-06-11

All HTTP 200. Fourteen consecutive years, thirteen of them within three weeks
of the start of the camp season. A separate capture of /index.html exists for
2004-12-07, and 2003-02-04 and 2008-01-18 captures exist off-June.

THE SUCCESSOR DOMAIN, ymcaquebec.org, is archived from 2009-08-10. Its
/en/camps path has a capture at 2025-11-08. The two together should cover the
rebrand.

=====================================================================
WHAT COULD NOT BE DONE FROM HERE, AND WHY
=====================================================================

THE INTERIOR CAMP PAGES CANNOT BE LOCATED BY GUESSING. Every one of these
returned NO CAPTURE at all:

  /camps · /en/camps · /kanawana · /camp_kanawana · /en/kanawana ·
  /camps/kanawana · /en

That is evidence about the guesses and NOT about whether camp pages were
captured -- the same trap that the Carol Skinner inventory hit an hour
earlier. A site's menu labels rarely match its URLs, and this one was
bilingual, which doubles the ways a path can differ from an English guess.

THE REAL PATHS ARE IN THE NAVIGATION OF THE CAPTURES THEMSELVES, and reading a
capture needs web.archive.org, which is blocked here at both ports and cannot
be reached with a headless browser either (f_5362). SO THIS IS AN OPERATOR
TASK, and its first step is one click: open the 2003 or 2004 front page and
read the menu.

=====================================================================
WHAT TO LOOK FOR, IN ROUGH ORDER OF VALUE
=====================================================================

1. SESSION STRUCTURE AND DATES, year by year. The wiki's account of how
   Kanawana's sessions were shaped in the 2000s is thin and largely inferred.
2. FEES. This project has almost no price series after the 1970s.
3. THE DIRECTOR'S NAME in each season -- directors-index.md has gaps here.
4. AGE BANDS AND SECTION NAMES, which is how programme changes show up.
5. THE FRENCH PAGES. Kanawana ran a French section, and a bilingual site will
   often say more about it in French than in English.
6. CAMP OTOREKE AND ANY DAY CAMPS, for the same years.
7. The 2009-2012 stretch spans the move to ymcaquebec.org; the two domains
   side by side may date the rebrand precisely.

A NOTE ON WHAT NOT TO TRUST. A camp page captured in June advertises the
season about to happen, not the one that happened. Read the tense, exactly as
the 1904 Men of Montreal issue had to be read.
